issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to an interface named 'Rideable', but the solution implements an interface named 'Mountable' and has classes (Pig, Seal) implementing Mountable. This type/name mismatch between the expected interface and the solution will confuse students about which interface to create and implement, and it deviates from the UML/specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Ensure consistent interface naming across artifacts. Either rename the solution's 'Mountable' interface to 'Rideable' and have Pig and Seal implement Rideable, or update the problem statement and template to use 'Mountable' instead of 'Rideable'. Preferably align the solution with the problem UML by providing a 'Rideable' interface with messageOnRide().

issues.description: The solution repository contains a Rideable.java file that is effectively empty (no interface declaration or package), while the exercise and template expect a functional Rideable interface. An empty or missing Rideable implementation in the solution will cause confusion and compilation errors for students comparing artifacts.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a proper Rideable interface in the solution repository matching the specification (e.g., package declaration and 'public interface Rideable { String messageOnRide(); }') and update classes to implement it (or remove the empty Rideable.java if replacing it with Mountable and also update problem/template accordingly).

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to the rideable interface as 'Rideable', but the solution repository uses a different identifier 'Mountable' for the same concept (and leaves Rideable.java effectively empty). This naming divergence (Rideable vs Mountable) breaks the one-to-one mapping students expect between the exercise description/template and the reference solution, causing confusion when implementing or testing Rideable behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the interface name across artifacts. Rename the solution's 'Mountable' interface to 'Rideable' (and update all classes to implement Rideable), and remove or populate the empty Rideable.java so the interface name matches the problem statement and template. Alternatively, change the problem/template references to 'Mountable' consistently, but prefer renaming the solution to 'Rideable' to align with the exercise description.
